_description: Intro slides, shown in order after the title screen. Each slide has a 'caption' (the text in the box under the picture; write \n for a line break) and an 'illustration' (which built-in pixel picture to show). Built-in pictures: "valley-home" (Alex waving at the garden gate of their fenced cottage), "town-meeting" (neighbors outside the town hall looking at the data center plan), "construction" (bulldozers clearing the woods, a steel frame going up), "data-center-opens" (the finished data center lit up at dusk). Add, remove or reorder slides freely; a picture can be used more than once. 'music' (optional) = which track from audio.json plays during the slides.
_usedIn: Simulation page → Intro slides (between the title screen and '6 months later')

slides.caption: This is Alex. He has lived in Datadew Valley for his entire life. For Alex, Datadew Valley represents community; gardening with his neighbors, fishing with his family and attending city hall meetings to help envision a better future for the people he cares so deeply about.

One spring, Datadew’s mayor struck a deal with Big Data, an AI company hoping to create a data center to power their AI platform. Uninformed community members gathered outside the town hall as the mayor assured everyone jobs, money and prosperity would come with the data center.

Within weeks, bulldozers cleared the woods by Alex's house. A road was constructed along the river that Alex once called a place of respite. Trucks brought construction material, creating dust and smog that clouded Alex's vision of what he once called home.

By autumn the data center was finished. Alex could never sleep, as the lights of the data center shined too bright. A low hum settled over the valley, a place unrecognizable with Big Data's intervention.
